evidence.title: William Beaudine
evidence.text: William Washington Beaudine (January 15, 1892 – March 18, 1970) was an American film actor and director.

evidence.title: William Beaudine
evidence.text: He was one of Hollywood's most prolific directors, turning out films in remarkable numbers and in a wide variety of genres.

evidence.title: Penrod and Sam (1931 film)
evidence.text: Penrod and Sam is a 1931 American Pre-Code comedy film directed by William Beaudine and starring Leon Janney and Frank Coghlan Jr. It is an adaptation of the novel "Penrod and Sam" by Booth Tarkington.

evidence.title: Penrod and Sam (1931 film)
evidence.text: Beaudine had previously directed a 1923 silent version "Penrod and Sam", and was invited to remake his earlier success.

evidence.title: Cornered (1924 film)
evidence.text: Cornered is a 1924 American silent drama film directed by William Beaudine.

evidence.title: Cornered (1924 film)
evidence.text: It is considered to be a lost.

evidence.title: Cornered (1924 film)
evidence.text: The story was filmed again in 1930, this time as a talkie called "Road to Paradise".

evidence.title: Cornered (1924 film)
evidence.text: It was also directed by Beaudine.

evidence.title: Adventures of Kitty O'Day
evidence.text: Adventures of Kitty O'Day is a 1945 American comedy mystery film directed by William Beaudine and starring Jean Parker, Peter Cookson and Tim Ryan.

evidence.title: Adventures of Kitty O'Day
evidence.text: It was a sequel to the 1944 film "Detective Kitty O'Day".

evidence.title: Adventures of Kitty O'Day
evidence.text: The two films were an attempt to create a new detective series but no further films were made.

evidence.title: Adventures of Kitty O'Day
evidence.text: A third film, "Fashion Model", also directed by Beaudine, was made using a similar formula but with another actress playing a heroine with a different name.

evidence.title: Richard Benjamin
evidence.text: Richard Samuel Benjamin (born May 22, 1938) is an American actor and film director.

evidence.title: Boy of Mine
evidence.text: Boy of Mine is a 1923 American silent family drama film directed by William Beaudine.

evidence.title: Boy of Mine
evidence.text: It stars Ben Alexander, Rockliffe Fellowes, and Henry B. Walthall.

evidence.title: Boy of Mine
evidence.text: Wendy L. Marshall stated that "Beaudine had the Midas touch when it came to directing children" in films like this and "Penrod and Sam".

evidence.title: Road to Paradise (film)
evidence.text: Road to Paradise is a 1930 American pre-Code drama film produced and distributed by First National Pictures, and starring Loretta Young, Jack Mulhall and Raymond Hatton.

evidence.title: Road to Paradise (film)
evidence.text: It was directed by William Beaudine and is based on a 1920 play Dodson Mitchell by Zelda Sears called "Cornered".

evidence.title: Road to Paradise (film)
evidence.text: The film was a remake of a 1924 silent version, entitled "Cornered", which was also directed by William Beaudine.

evidence.title: Men in Her Life
evidence.text: Men in Her Life is a 1931 American Pre-Code drama film directed by William Beaudine and starring Lois Moran, Charles Bickford and Victor Varconi.

evidence.title: Men in Her Life
evidence.text: It was based on a novel by Warner Fabian (Samuel Hopkins Adams).

evidence.title: Men in Her Life
evidence.text: It was made during a brief spell Beaudine had working at Columbia Pictures.

evidence.title: Men in Her Life
evidence.text: Critics considered the film one of the studio's better B releases.

evidence.title: Men in Her Life
evidence.text: Part of the film was set in the Café de la Paix in Paris which was reconstructed authentically at the Columbia studios.

evidence.title: Men in Her Life
evidence.text: Columbia also made a Spanish-language version of this film, entitled "Hombres en mi vida".

evidence.title: Clancy Street Boys
evidence.text: Clancy Street Boys is a 1943 film directed by William Beaudine and starring the East Side Kids.

evidence.title: Clancy Street Boys
evidence.text: It is Beaudine's first film with the team; he would direct several more in the series and many in the Bowery Boys canon.

evidence.title: Clancy Street Boys
evidence.text: Leo Gorcey married the female lead Amelita Ward.

evidence.title: Clancy Street Boys
evidence.text: There is no mention of "Clancy Street" in the film, but a rival gang at Cherry Street appears at the beginning and climax of the film.

evidence.title: Billy the Kid Versus Dracula
evidence.text: Billy the Kid vs. Dracula is a 1966 American low-budget horror-Western film directed by William Beaudine.

evidence.title: Billy the Kid Versus Dracula
evidence.text: It was released theatrically as part of a double bill, along with "Jesse James Meets Frankenstein's Daughter".

evidence.title: Billy the Kid Versus Dracula
evidence.text: Both films were shot in eight days at Corriganville Movie Ranch and at Paramount Studios in mid 1965; both were the final feature films of director William Beaudine.

evidence.title: Billy the Kid Versus Dracula
evidence.text: The film revolves around Billy the Kid played by stuntman Chuck Courtney trying to save his fiancee from Dracula (John Carradine repeating his role from the low-budget Universal Studios movie sequels to the Bela Lugosi classic).

evidence.title: Billy the Kid Versus Dracula
evidence.text: The films were produced by television producer Carroll Case for Joseph E. Levine.
